content: Have you ever wondered why we don't wear a thick woollen sweater in the hot summer, or just a thin cotton t-shirt in the freezing winter? Imagine trying to play outside in the snow wearing just shorts! Brrr!
Why do you think animals like bears and dogs don't need to wear clothes like we do? What would happen if we didn't have clothes to wear when it rains?

content.title: Our Body's Shield
content.description: Just like a house protects us from the rain and wind, clothes protect our body. Think of clothes as a special shield we wear!

content: We wear clothes to cover our bodies and protect ourselves from heat, cold, rain, and dust. The clothes we wear change based on the weather, season, and occasion.

definition: A time of the year that has a specific type of weather, like summer, winter, or monsoon.
A soft, fluffy material that comes from the cotton plant, used to make cool clothes for summer.
Thick hair from animals like sheep, used to make warm clothes for winter.

question: Which of these is the main reason we wear clothes?
options: To protect our body from heat, cold, and rain

content: Explain to your younger sibling or friend why they need to wear a raincoat when they go out in the rain instead of a cotton shirt. Try teaching them what you just learned!
Encourage the child to touch different fabrics around the house, like a cotton towel, a woolen sweater, and a plastic raincoat, to feel the difference.
Clothes are just like the fur on a polar bear or the shell on a turtle. In science, we learn about how animals adapt to their environment. Humans use clothes to adapt to any environment in the world!
Some people think we get wool from plants, but wool actually comes from animals like sheep and rabbits! Cotton comes from plants.

Go to your wardrobe and find one piece of clothing for summer (like a t-shirt), one for winter (like a jacket), and one for the rain (like a raincoat). Lay them on your bed and touch them to see how different they feel!
